Has anyone else read it? I thought it was okayish, but still found it disappointing compared to its predecessors, some reasons being

  • No more monsters: Many of the previous books most thrilling moments were based around Artyom having a run-in with those creatures who had made their home in the irradiated ruins of Moscow. Glukovsky's explanation that those basically died out because the the surface radiation increased in strength is rather lackluster, doubly so because even then, there still should be various abberations stalking the metro tunnels. The setting generally drifts away from the pseudo-supernatural elements of the other two and instead fully focuses on humans acting as monsters.

  • Disappointing Ending: I didn't really mind that some of the Metro inhabitants thought that the radio jammers were for their own best, and that the Americans still were in any capacity to nuke them, but the fact that literally everyone in the Metro save for Artyom, Anja, Ljocha (that slimy traitor) and that one Reich writer blindly accepted this as a fact when the Metro itself shows any survivors would be busy killing each other was downright sad, even if you accept the moral of the story.

  • Pacing Problems: Although things do speed up quite rapidly near the ending, the book starts of relatively slow, with some encounters (i.e. Artyoms first stay in that station-sized brothel) having a rather gratutious length.
